the Hawking radiation is obtained by using only covariant (and gauge invariant) boundary conditions and that this approach is related to the Unruh vacuum.

the Hawking radiation can be obtained from the effective action using only covariant conditions at the event horizons; the connection with Unruh vacuum and recent analysis using anomaly is established; the effective action is derived for the case of charged black holes; the Hawking radiation is obtained in the case of Reissner-Nordstrom black hole.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the study of the Hawking radiation in the context of the effective action.
the derivation of Hawking radiation from black holes in an approach that is based on the effective action and covariant boundary condition, and is independent of the Unruh effect.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Hawking radiation from the event horizon of a charged black hole is derived using only covariant and consistent boundary conditions at the horizon.
Hawking radiation is the consequence of a covariant anomaly at the event horizon, and the effective action is the source of the anomaly.
Hawking radiation is a covariant effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effective action approach, together with covariant boundary conditions, is an efficient tool to derive Hawking radiation from a black hole.
the Hawking radiation is the effect of the quantum field theory on the black holes and the Hawking temperature is the temperature of the black hole.
we have derived the Hawking radiation using only boundary conditions and the effective actions, and the connection with the anomaly analysis is established.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hawking radiation can be derived without using the Unruh vacuum.
the Hawking radiation can be derived without any reference to a specific form of the effective action.
, for the purpose of calculating the Hawking radiation, it is sufficient to use the covariant boundary conditions alone and the effective action need not be explicitly calculated.
